{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.",
    "If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slope or add upward bias.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a lagged correction or dampen momentum.",
    "When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., rapid drop from 65+ to 55+), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with recent volatility history.",
    "If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is volatile, consider short-term downward adjustment to reflect sentiment uncertainty.",
    "For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from model’s initial forecast, re-evaluate baseline assumption and apply sentiment-weighted correction.",
    "If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model may be overfitting trend; apply smoothing or stochastic correction to avoid overconfidence in direction."
  ]
}
